newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY-WIESE,LE ROUX DROPPED BY NEW SAFRICA COACH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY-WIESE,LE ROUX DROPPED BY NEW SAFRICA COACH.

text.p: Carel du Plessis has dropped World Cup winning pair Hennie le Roux and Kobus Wiese from the South African side to meet Tonga in Cape Town on June 10.

The new Springbok coach also made four other changes, two of them forced by injury from the side which ended last season on a high with a 37-20 win over Wales, when he announced his first squad in Johannesburg on Monday.

The Gauteng lions (formerly Transvaal) pair, who were also regulars in South Africa's 1996 season-ending run of six successive victories, were the most notable absentees when du Plessis named 27 players who will also go on to face the touring British Lions.
Le Roux is replaced at centre by the uncapped and relatively unknown Griqualand West centre Edrich Lubbe, while lock Krynauw Otto wins his fourth cap in place of Wiese.

Prop Dawie Theron is replaced by fit-again Os du Randt and hooker Naka Drotski is replaced by James Dalton in the other voluntary changes from the final side named by du Plessis' predecessor Andre Markgraaff.
The injured duo of lock Mark Andrews and winger Jacques Olivier are replaced by Fritz van Heerden and Andre Snyman respectively.
The first of three tests against the British Lions is also in Cape Town on June 21.

South Africa - 15 Andre Joubert, 4 James Small, 13 Japie Mulder, 12 Edrich Lubbe, 11 Andre Snyman, 10 Henry Honiball, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen, 8 Gary Teichmann (captain), 7 Andre Venter, 6 Ruben Kruger, 5 Krynauw Otto, 4 Fritz van Heerden, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2 Naka Drotske, 1 Os du Randt.
Replacements: Russell Bennett, Botha Wessels, Werner Swanepoel, Hannes Strydom, James Dalton, Dawie Theron.
Additional players: Marius Hurter, Mark Andrews, Johan Erasmus, Justin Swart, Percival Montgomery and Pieter Muller.
